explanation: Survivorship curves are classified into three major types: 1) Type I: characteristic of populations in which most individuals survive past the midpoint of their lifespan, with mortality occurring primarily at the end of the lifespan. 2) Type II: death occurs at a linear rate over time, meaning the probability of death is unrelated to age. 3) Type III: characteristic of populations in which the vast majority of individuals die at a very young age.

questions.q: What is the defining characteristic of a Type I survivorship curve?
opts: Most individuals die at a young age.
The death rate is linear and completely independent of age.
Most individuals survive past the midpoint of the lifespan, with death occurring near the end.
Individuals have unlimited reproductive opportunities throughout life.
questions.exp: Type I is defined as 'Characteristic of a population in which most individuals survive past the midpoint of the life span and death does not come until the end of the life span.'

questions.q: Which type of survivorship curve exhibits a linear death rate over time, unrelated to the age of the individuals?
questions.exp: Type II is characterized by 'Death is linear over time (unrelated to age).'
